the preoxidation process can be used to produce an Al2O3 scale which is resistant to sulphidation in environments of high H2S and low oxygen activities, provided that the scale remains mechanically intact.
the transport of sulphur to the alloy/scale interfaces in these environments is the controlling factor in the breakdown of Al2O3 scale.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preoxidation treatment of iron-base alloys to develop Al2O3 rich scales improves the subsequent sulphidability of the alloys, provided that the scale remains intact.

preoxidation of iron-base alloys containing chromium, aluminum and yttrium in H2/H 2O mixtures to form external Al2O 3-rich scales is an effective means for improving sulphidation resistance in environments of low oxygen activity at high temperatures.
the transport of sulphur in Al2O3 scale is a major factor in determining the long-term sulphidation resistance of alloys such as Fe-27%Cr-4%Al and similar Fe-Cr-Al alloys containing yttria additions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sulphur penetration is a major factor that limits the long-term sulphidation resistance of Al2O3-forming alloys in high sulphur environments at high temperatures.
the use of preformed Al2S3 scale on Fe-Cr-Al alloys can provide a very high resistance to sulphidation in environments of low oxygen activity and relatively high sulphur activity.

the use of preformed Al2S2 scales on alloys such as Fe-27%Cr-4%Al can provide good resistance to sulphidation in environments of high SO2 and low oxygen activity, but only for a limited period of time.
